Generate one three-layer synthetic sample for encoder pretraining

Source: R/catalog_generation.R
generate_noisy_pretrain_sample.Rd

Builds a synthetic GC-DMS image by stacking three layers of peaks:

Usage

generate_noisy_pretrain_sample(
  catalog,
  H,
  W,
  anchor_ids,
  variable_config = NULL,
  contamination_config = NULL,
  add_noise = TRUE,
  size_jitter = 0.15,
  location_jitter_rt = 2,
  location_jitter_cv = 1,
  noise_scale = 1,
  anchor_dropout = 0,
  anchor_jitter_variability = NULL,
  variable_source_peak_params = NULL,
  peak_shape = c("gaussian", "emg", "mix"),
  emg_tau_range = c(0.2, 0.8),
  emg_mix_prob = 0.3,
  anchor_draw = c("all", "prevalence")
)

Arguments

catalog

A peak_catalog object.

H, W

Output image dimensions in pixels.

anchor_ids

Integer vector of compound_ids to force-fire. Typically the ~100 anchors from the universal catalog with prevalence >= 0.9.

variable_config

Optional list controlling the variable layer. Fields:

  • draw: how compounds are chosen from the eligible pool. "uniform" (default, the original behaviour) draws n_per_sample of them uniformly without replacement, so every eligible compound appears in about n / length(eligible) of images whatever its own prevalence. "prevalence" fires each eligible compound independently with probability min(1, prevalence * prevalence_scale) (the same Bernoulli rule as generate_one_synthetic_from_catalog()), so the expected count is the sum of those probabilities and per-compound frequencies match the catalog. Needs a prevalence column.

  • prevalence_scale: non-negative multiplier on catalog prevalence in "prevalence" mode. Default 1. Ignored in "uniform" mode.

  • n_per_sample: scalar (fixed count) or length-2 numeric (uniform range). In "uniform" mode, how many variable compounds to draw; default c(30, 80). In "prevalence" mode, an optional per-sample cap: when more compounds fire than the cap, a uniform subset of that size is kept. Default NULL (no cap); a cap below the expected count biases frequencies back toward uniform.

  • prevalence_range: length-2 numeric giving the catalog prevalence range eligible for the variable pool. Default c(0.05, 0.5).

  • intensity_scale: length-2 numeric giving amplitude multiplier bounds. Default c(0.3, 1.0) (variable compounds slightly dimmer than anchors on average).

  • exclude_anchors: TRUE (default) — remove anchor_ids from the variable pool so anchors don't get drawn twice. Pass NULL to skip this layer.

contamination_config

Optional list controlling contamination injection. Same fields as off_catalog_peaks in simulate_case_control_from_catalog() except with n_per_sample instead of n_cases / n_controls. Default field values: n_per_sample = c(5, 30), rt_range / cv_range = 5-95% of the catalog's (median) unpadded data block expressed as canvas fractions (5-95% of the canvas for catalogs without data dims), intensity_range = c(0.1, 0.5), exclusion_eps_rt = 0.02, exclusion_eps_cv = 0.05. Pass NULL to skip this layer. The exclusion boxes surround every catalog compound position, not only the compounds placed in this sample, so they do not depend on the anchor / variable draw. Note that these defaults are much brighter and more exclusive than real off-catalog peaks: on a 606-sample universal catalog, real off-catalog peaks had median normalised intensity about 0.014 (90th percentile about 0.042) against the default intensity_range = c(0.1, 0.5), and the default exclusion boxes confine contamination to the gaps between compounds (only 61 of 96 CV columns reachable on a 1504 x 96 grid). For realistic clutter consider intensity_range near c(0.005, 0.05) and smaller boxes (e.g. exclusion_eps_rt = 0.002, exclusion_eps_cv = 0.01).

add_noise

Whether to add folded-Normal background noise on top of the three layers.

size_jitter, location_jitter_rt, location_jitter_cv

Per-peak jitter parameters (same convention as generate_one_synthetic_from_catalog()).

noise_scale

Multiplier on catalog noise SD.

anchor_dropout

Per-sample Bernoulli probability of dropping each anchor before rendering. 0 (default) fires all anchors.

anchor_jitter_variability

Optional length-2 range for a per-sample scalar multiplier on location_jitter_rt/cv. NULL (default) uses the fixed jitter values as-is.

variable_source_peak_params

Optional peak_params bundle. When provided, the variable layer is rendered via generate_one_synthetic() on this bundle (real peaks, empirical locations, joint attributes) instead of the catalog-clustered render. Mutually exclusive with variable_config.

anchor_draw

How anchors fire. "all" (default) fires every anchor, minus anchor_dropout. "prevalence" fires each anchor independently with probability prevalence * (1 - anchor_dropout), so anchors at prevalence 0.8 are absent from about 20% of images, as in real samples. Needs a prevalence column.

Value

List with clean (H x W), noisy (H x W), and per-layer composition metadata (anchor_ids, variable_ids, contamination_positions, and rendered_ids — the compound_ids actually drawn in the anchors / variable layers, used as ground-truth presence labels).

Details

  1. Anchor backbone. Every compound in anchor_ids fires (subject to anchor_dropout / anchor_draw), with its own catalog morphology and normal per-peak location / size jitter. These are the stable ~100 highly-prevalent compounds you want the encoder to treat as the baseline landscape.

  2. Variable catalog compounds (optional). Per-sample random subset of the catalog's less-prevalent compounds — filtered by variable_config$prevalence_range and (optionally) excluding the anchor pool. Simulates diet-related, host-genetics-related, and other per-person volatiles. Intensity scaled by a per-peak factor drawn from variable_config$intensity_scale. The subset is drawn uniformly (every eligible compound equally likely) or, with variable_config$draw = "prevalence", each compound fires at its own catalog prevalence.

  3. Contamination (optional). Uniform-random peaks placed at positions NOT overlapping catalog compounds. Simulates sampling apparatus contamination, environmental exposure, and truly unfamiliar peaks. Sigmas drawn from the pooled catalog sigma distribution so shapes look realistic.
